assumptions: The constitution and accepted SDD-001 remain authoritative and are not implicitly amended by this draft.
All line references refer to docs/specs/SDD-OBS-001/spec.md.
Plan prose and the round-1 resolution claim were considered context, not substitutes for normative requirements.
Counterexamples are specification-level scenarios, not claims of observed implementation defects.
No files were modified, tests executed, tasks created or external systems mutated.
blocking_questions: R2-01 — BQ-02: Required-gate selection remains underdefined (spec lines 76–106). Missing contract: the authoritative changed-surface baseline, applicability semantics and ordering of synthetic legacy gates. Counterexample: a file changed earlier on a feature branch is unchanged relative to HEAD but changed relative to the integration base; two planners select different mandatory gates. Two unmapped commands also have no profile declaration order. Smallest decision: define the baseline and dirty/untracked/deleted-path treatment, applicability matching rules, and deterministic synthetic gate identity/order. Define exact command mapping so argument order, quoting or normalization cannot collapse commands with different behavior.

R2-02 — BQ-03: File-set and symlink semantics are incomplete (lines 155–182). Missing contract: glob dialect, case handling, directory-link traversal and inclusion of in-repository referent contents. Counterexample: the only declared input is config/current.json, a symlink to config/version.json; changing version.json leaves the required link-target hash unchanged although the command reads different bytes. Different glob implementations can also omit different files while each claims deterministic matching. Smallest decision: specify matching/canonicalization rules and require all result-sensitive referent contents to participate, or make such gates non-cacheable. Explicitly require complete declaration of result-sensitive inputs rather than only hashing whatever was declared.

R2-03 — BQ-03/BQ-12: Invocation-mode fingerprints conflict with continuation reuse (lines 160, 68–70 and AC-OBS-007). Counterexample: integration gates A and B pass and C fails. A continuation uses identical files and policy, but the required mode dimension changes from integration to continuation; exact fingerprints cannot match, so A and B cannot be reused as AC-OBS-007 expects. Smallest decision: define whether continuation retains the originating verification policy identity or uses an explicit compatibility rule. State which cross-mode evidence is eligible while preserving task-completion freshness.

R2-04 — BQ-01/BQ-05: Freshness of task-command preconditions remains ambiguous (lines 62–88 and 224–232). Counterexample: a task declares a consumer command whose profile dependency initializes required local state. The task command runs freshly, but its dependency is reused from another worktree without recreating that state. Literal task-command freshness holds while its intended precondition does not. Smallest decision: explicitly choose whether task-completion freshness extends to dependencies; if dependencies may be reused, define which preconditions must be represented by retained artifacts or probes and when dependency execution is mandatory.

R2-05 — BQ-05: Artifact byte identity and producer-context identity are not reconciled (lines 224–232). Counterexample: a focused run or copied file replaces full-test output with identical bytes. Producer evidence and current hashes satisfy the listed reuse conditions, but the replacement rule says the full producer must run again. Artifact paths also lack an explicit containment rule comparable to manual reports. Smallest decision: state whether byte-identical restoration is valid, or require a producer-attempt/context binding that replacement invalidates; define containment and symlink rules for produced/consumed artifact paths.

R2-06 — BQ-06: Retry prohibition does not clearly span automatically created attempts (lines 236–248). Counterexample: after a critical gate fails, a wrapper creates a new verification run id and invokes it again automatically. Each attempt contains one process invocation, yet this masks failure through attempt rollover. Smallest decision: explicitly prohibit automatic re-attempt of the same failed critical verification scope, define what constitutes explicit human authorization across entry points, and distinguish permitted new builder work from retrying unchanged failed verification. Specify that reports expose the earlier failure alongside a later PASS.

R2-07 — BQ-07: Serialization scope and drift guarantees conflict or leave gaps (lines 184–185, 252–268 and 431). Counterexample: two different profile snapshots execute concurrently in one repository and overwrite the same artifact; the per-repository-plus-snapshot locks allow this despite the statement that execution remains serialized. Separately, an input changes A→B→A during a command, so pre/post equality holds although the result used B. Smallest decision: settle serialization across profiles sharing a repository/artifacts and define whether transient mutations must be prevented/detected or are explicitly outside the supported execution model. Endpoint equality alone cannot establish the stated changed-input invariant.

R2-08 — BQ-08: Manual report validation still lacks an authoritative identity contract (lines 296–319 and 414). Missing contract: canonical marker syntax/verdict vocabulary, checkpoint existence and relationship to the reviewed scope, and dirty-review handling. Counterexample: a report and CLI both contain the same arbitrary 40-hex value, or a report reviews dirty changes while naming an unchanged commit; the stated equality checks accept it. A Markdown example containing marker-like text also has no specified parsing outcome. Smallest decision: define one report binding format and duplicate-marker behavior, validate the checkpoint against the intended repository/review scope, and explicitly permit or reject dirty-tree evidence with the necessary identity. Settle whether the same report registered under different task/role metadata is a distinct observation or a conflict.

R2-09 — BQ-10: First-pass and rework metrics remain ambiguous for incomplete and repeated observations (lines 323–345). Counterexample: the first builder attempt has legacy provenance without an attempt field and the second has complete v2 PASS evidence; excluding the legacy record could falsely report first-pass success. Two required reviewers rejecting before one subsequent builder attempt could count as one or two rework cycles. Manual registration also does not identify whether an observation was required or accepted for time_to_independent_pass. Smallest decision: define unknown-first-attempt behavior, rework deduplication/grouping, observation ordering, and the source of required/accepted status. Define whether a later verification resume can make the original builder attempt count as first-pass.

R2-10 — BQ-13: Secret handling has unresolved conflicts between allowed hashes/paths and prohibited secret-bearing values (lines 399–416). Counterexample: a secret appears in a report filename or a tool version probe, both allowed structured fields; another appears in a command argument whose command hash is required even though hashes of secret-bearing opaque values are prohibited. Smallest decision: define rejection/redaction rules for identifiers, relative paths, probes and diagnostics, and explicitly distinguish permitted whole-artifact hashes from forbidden secret-derived values. Extend the seeded-secret criterion to these channels so the verification author need not invent the boundary.

R2-11 — BQ-14: The performance requirement is measurable but internally underspecified (lines 426–429). Counterexample: 100 gates all match the same 5,000 files versus 100 disjoint selections have the same declared workload size but radically different manifest work; file sizes are also unbounded. Strict linearity in DAG size plus distinct paths omits total matched gate/path associations and bytes hashed. Smallest decision: define the benchmark fixture's file sizes and overlap, timing boundary and CI measurement procedure, and express complexity in the actual input dimensions or narrow the linearity claim.
findings: BQ-01 — Original conflict resolved: spec lines 62–66 and AC-OBS-001 explicitly preserve fresh execution of every task-declared command. The dependency-precondition extension remains open under R2-04; it is not a claim that accepted SDD-001 already requires fresh execution of every profile dependency.

BQ-02 — Partially resolved: union, transitive dependency closure, mandatory legacy execution, INVALIDATED→RUN and stop-on-failure behavior are normative. Selection/mapping/order boundaries remain under R2-01.

BQ-03 — Partially resolved: cwd, dirty/untracked files, policy, tool probes, non-hermetic environment and repository reuse boundaries are addressed. R2-02 and R2-03 prevent a complete fingerprint/reuse contract.

BQ-04 — Resolved at specification level: trusted producer, provider-write threat, terminal evidence requirements, unsupported/partial evidence rejection and recoverable corruption are explicit. A hostile arbitrary local writer is explicitly excluded.
BQ-05 — Partially resolved: missing or mismatched coverage material forces regeneration. Byte-identical replacement, producer context and artifact boundaries remain under R2-04/R2-05.

BQ-06 — Partially resolved: internal retry controls and later human-authorized PASS with immutable failure history are explicit. Cross-attempt automatic retry and summary interpretation remain under R2-06/R2-09.
BQ-07 — Partially resolved: terminal publication boundaries and index reconstruction are explicit. Cross-profile serialization and transient drift remain under R2-07.
BQ-08 — Partially resolved: telemetry-only authority, report hashes and repeat/conflict behavior are substantially specified. Canonical parsing and authoritative reviewed identity remain under R2-08.
BQ-09 — Resolved at specification level: runner/orchestrator bind control policy, later policy changes require replanning, and direct CLI rejects dirty/untracked active policy by default.
BQ-10 — Partially resolved: counting units, unknown cost and coverage reporting are explicit. Mixed-history first-pass, rework grouping and required/accepted observation semantics remain under R2-09.

BQ-11 — Resolved for compatibility/rollback: v1 remains readable but cannot authorize reuse; unsupported versions cannot authorize reuse; derived cache and audit history are separated. Mixed-version metric interpretation remains a BQ-10 issue.

BQ-12 — Substantially resolved: machine categories, CLI exits, corrupt-cache recovery and entry-point parity are normative. Orchestration metadata cannot legitimately change equivalent fingerprints. R2-03 must still reconcile mode-sensitive fingerprints with continuation.
BQ-13 — Partially resolved: structured allowlisting, raw-data exclusions and seeded-secret tests are present. Allowed-field and hash boundary decisions remain under R2-10.
BQ-14 — Partially resolved: documentation artifacts and omission behavior are explicit. Benchmark/complexity acceptance remains under R2-11.
No prototype is justified: the remaining questions require contract decisions, not empirical selection between architectures.
non_blocking_risks: BQ-09 now normatively requires control-repository policy selection and explicit replanning after policy changes. Architecture review should verify that execution checks the live authoritative policy rather than merely comparing a captured snapshot to itself.

BQ-12 resolves ordinary corrupt-cache recovery versus fatal exit 2: corruption is diagnostic when fresh execution is safe and fatal only when safe reconstruction/execution is impossible. Stable recovery guidance should accompany the outcome categories.

The handbook source/output and SDD-OBS-001-specific manual telemetry obligation are explicit. The general SHOULD and feature closure requirement are scoped differently and do not inherently contradict each other.
Conservative reuse eligibility may reduce performance; this is acceptable until measured improvements preserve the accepted safety contract.
residual_risks: Implementation, architecture and runtime correctness were not assessed.
Architecture Grill and the independently authored verification contract remain required after specification convergence.
The remaining ambiguities can change acceptance outcomes; task generation should remain blocked pending their resolution.
summary: The revision resolves the original mandatory re-execution conflict and several provenance, compatibility and failure-policy questions. It does not yet provide an unambiguous contract for selection, fingerprinting, continuation, artifact provenance, manual evidence and metrics. Independent verification criteria would still require policy invention. This was a read-only Spec Grill; no architecture approval or prototype is recommended.
